title: Chapter 84 — Financing & The Money Conversation
intro: Promotional financing mechanics, the monthly bridge, and the budget conversation with dignity.

sections.title: Financing as a Selling Tool
sections.content:
Financing is not a last resort. It is a selling tool. Present it proactively on any ticket over $1,500. The customer who says 'that is a lot' often means 'I do not have that cash right now' — not 'I do not want it.'

Introduce it during Step 7, after the product is chosen. 'This comes to $3,200 for the package. We have 12-month no-interest financing — that breaks down to about $267 a month. Would that make the decision easier?'

sections.title: Framing That Works
sections.content:
Monthly: '$3,200 sounds like a lot. $89 a month for 36 months does not.' Daily: 'That is about $3 a day for a dishwasher that will last 10-15 years.' Per-use: 'If you run this dishwasher 5 times a week, that is about 12 cents per load.'

Financing makes step-ups painless. 'The difference between the 300 series and the 500 series is $400. On financing, that is an extra $33 a month. For that, you get CrystalDry.'

sections.title: Handling Declined Applications
sections.content:
Handle with dignity. 'No worries — let me see what we can do at your target budget. We have great options.' Never make them feel embarrassed. Never ask why they were declined. Simply move to the next solution.

Do not ask 'do you need financing?' — it implies they cannot afford it. Do not lead with financing before presenting value. Do not pressure the application. Do not assume older customers do not want financing — many prefer it for cash flow.
